holidays.name: National Mario Day
holidays.description: Gamers put on their red caps and celebrate Nintendo's mustachioed plumber. They play classic platformers, eat pasta and stomp a few Goombas. The date works because 'MAR10' looks a lot like 'Mario'.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial fan celebration. It grew out of the calendar pun on 'MAR10' and has been popular with Nintendo fans and the company itself for years.
holidays.funFact: Mario first appeared in 1981 in the arcade game Donkey Kong. He was called 'Jumpman' and worked as a carpenter, not a plumber.

holidays.name: National Blueberry Popover Day
holidays.description: This day honors the puffy, golden, airy popover with juicy blueberries baked into it. It's a breakfast treat that is crisp outside and custardy inside. Butter and jam are welcome.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. Its origin is unclear, but it fits the tradition of giving baked goods their own day.
holidays.funFact: Popovers get their dramatic rise from steam alone. They have no yeast or baking powder, so the batter puffs up and 'pops over' the edge of the pan.

holidays.name: International Bagpipe Day
holidays.description: This day celebrates the bagpipes, an instrument people either love or find very loud. Pipers and fans mark it with skirling tunes and appreciation for the music's long history.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is popular with piping communities and Celtic culture fans.
holidays.funFact: Bagpipes are much older than Scotland's association with them. Versions of the instrument were played across Europe, North Africa and the Middle East for centuries.
